faq: Do you build login from scratch?

No. Writing your own login is a common source of security holes. We use a well maintained library or service such as Auth.js, Supabase or Firebase Auth, chosen for your stack, so updates and fixes keep arriving.
Can you add login to an app that already has users?
Yes, but it needs care. We map your current user table, keep existing accounts working and test sign-in before and after. If passwords need to be reset, we plan that with you first.
Do the login tools cost money?
Most have a free tier that suits an early product. Paid plans are billed by the provider directly to you. We tell you the likely cost at your expected size before we choose one.
Which sign-in providers can you add?
Google comes with Standard. Apple, Microsoft and GitHub can be added as extras where each provider approves your app. We follow each provider's setup rules and consent screens.
desc:
SaaS authentication and user roles setup lets people create accounts, sign in safely and see only what belongs to them. Ecom Swift LLC adds sign-up, login, password reset and permission levels to your product using proven, maintained tools.

## What is authentication and role-based access?

Authentication proves who someone is: an email and password, a Google account or a one-time code. Authorization, often called roles or permissions, decides what that person may do once inside. A role-based system gives each account a label, such as owner, member or viewer, and the product checks that label before showing a page or returning data.

Both halves matter. Login without roles lets every customer see everything. Roles without careful login lets the wrong person claim a seat.

## Why getting login wrong is costly

Authentication is the one feature where a shortcut can end a young company. A home-made login may store passwords badly, skip email checks or leave reset links that never expire. A missing permission check can let one customer open another customer's records just by changing a number in the address bar.

Users also judge your product by how it greets them. A confusing sign-up, a reset email that never arrives or a locked-out account sends people away on the first visit, before they have seen the product at all.

## How good access control helps your product grow

Clear login lowers the number of people who give up at the door. A short form, email verification and a working reset link mean more sign-ups actually reach the first screen. Social login removes the need to invent another password, which suits people who are only trying your product.

Roles let you sell to teams. A company will not adopt a tool where every employee has full rights. Once owners can invite members and control who edits or only views, a single buyer can bring in a whole group. That is how a personal tool becomes a team tool.

## What a solid setup includes

- Sign-up and login with email and password, stored using a maintained, well-reviewed library.
- Password reset through a time-limited email link.
- Email verification before first use, so typos and fake addresses do not fill your user list.
- Protected pages and data endpoints that check the session on the server.
- Session timeouts and a clear sign-out.
- Optional Google login, with Apple or Microsoft available as extras.
- Roles such as admin, member and viewer, checked on both pages and data.
- Team workspaces with invitations for products used by groups.
- Optional two-step login with an authenticator app.
- A login history and the ability to sign out other devices.

## How we approach the work

We do not invent our own login. We choose a mature authentication tool that fits your stack, configure it carefully and connect it to your database. Then we walk through every page and endpoint and mark which roles may reach it. A page hidden by a button is not protected; the server has to refuse the request.

The Basic package covers email login, reset, verification and protected pages. Standard adds Google login, two roles and an account settings page. Premium adds custom roles, team invitations, optional two-step login, login history and security notes. You receive working code, a short guide and a plain list of the rules we set.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Write down who should see and change what before any code is touched.
- Verify email addresses before granting access.
- Use the least access that lets each role do its work.
- Test every role by signing in as that role.
- Keep login tools updated.

**Avoid:**
- Building password storage yourself.
- Relying on hidden menu items instead of server checks.
- Sharing one account between teammates.
- Sending reset links that never expire.
- Adding a dozen roles before you need more than two.

## Who this service is for

Founders with a prototype that has no real login yet will get a safe foundation. Products with existing users that want to add teams or admin rights need careful changes that do not lock anyone out. Builders using a generated starter project can have the access rules reviewed and tightened before real customers arrive.

## What we need from you

Share your code repository or project, a short description of your user types, and your preferred sign-in providers. We work as a developer or collaborator and never ask for passwords. Some login providers need an account of their own, which you create and own; we guide you through it and set it up with you.
